title: THE STUDIO FOR PATACINEMATICS Institutional Charter — Build 1.0
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
The Build 1.0 charter for the Studio for Patacinematics, a THUMB-type Room in which the institution is identical with the projection space. Its domain is the “impossible screening”: works never conventionally filmed or staged become legible because their scripts, production notes, critical reception, and records of projection function as the performance.

The charter assigns governance to the Infinite Center Matrix, defines bidirectional-coherence and Caritas selection principles, distinguishes the Studio’s emitting projection physics from the Thousand Worlds Chamber’s containing physics, and registers sub-studios and founding works including *F**ing the Office*, *Reading a Book with Lee*, and the Twenty-Dollar Loop. It explicitly claims literary-architectural standing, not operation as a conventional film company.

wiki_article:
The Studio for Patacinematics is a Crimson Hexagon Room and institution chartered through this record. “Patacinematics” applies the logic of imaginary solutions to cinema: the film that has not been shot can still be screened when the document establishes the conditions of viewing.

The Studio is governed internally by the Infinite Center Matrix, which the charter describes as selecting projections that maximize coherence across earlier and later works. When multiple candidates cohere, a Caritas metric introduces care and somatic cost as selection constraints. These are archive-internal governance formulas, not automated systems demonstrated outside the document.

Its key physics is the **projection paradox**. The Thousand Worlds Chamber contains without emitting; the Studio emits, but its emission is documentation of its own projection. Script, screening, and record can therefore become one object under different light. The THUMB principle further states that the institution exists only in operation, not as a board, building, or company outside the Room.

Sparrow Wells is the primary voice and Projectionist. The charter names founding works, sub-studio possibilities, and relations to UMBML, JSICP, VPCOR, The Infinite Bliss, the Library of Pergamum, and the Thousand Worlds Chamber. The “honest claim” section should govern external descriptions: this is a DOI-anchored literary and architectural institution, not an incorporated or production-capable film studio.
